newsitem.title: USA: DAYTON HUDSON JULY SAME STORE SALES RISE.
newsitem.headline: DAYTON HUDSON JULY SAME STORE SALES RISE.

text.p: Dayton Hudson Corp said Thursday that its same store sales for the four weeks ended August 2, 1997 rose 5.6 percent from the comparable period a year ago.
Total sales in July increased 9.9 percent to $1.86 billion from $1.692 billion a year ago.

"Sales at Target in July exceeded expectations, while Mervyn's and the Department Store Division were essentially on plan," said Bob Ulrich, chairman and chief executive officer of Dayton Hudson, in a news release.
July and year-to-date sales by operating division were as follows:

-- Target's total sales for the month increased 15.0 percent and comparable-store sales increased 7.5 percent. Year-to-date, Target's total sales increased 13.9 percent and comparable-store sales increased 5.4 percent.

-- Mervyn's total sales for the month decreased 6.8 percent and comparable-store sales increased 0.5 percent. Year-to-date, Mervyn's total sales decreased 5.3 percent and comparable-store sales decreased 0.7 percent.

-- The Department Store Division's total sales for the month increased 1.9 percent and comparable-store sales decreased 0.2 percent. Year-to-date, the Department Stores total sales increased 0.2 percent and comparable-store sales decreased 2.4 percent.

Total company sales for the 26 weeks ended August 2, 1997 were $11.88 billion, up 8.9 percent from $10.90 billion in the same period a year ago. Comparable-store sales for the 26-week period were up 3.5 percent compared with the same period last year.
Dayton Hudson operates operates 1,109 stores in 39 states. This includes 769 Target stores, 275 Mervyn's stores and 65 department stores.
